title: New preprint: Dismantling chromosomal stasis across the eukaryotic tree of life
body: Megan Copeland, Meghann McConnell, Andres Barboza, and a large team of CURE undergraduates and lab members posted a new bioRxiv preprint quantifying dysploidy rates across 63,682 karyotypes in 55 eukaryotic clades. We show rates vary 844-fold and that even birds — the textbook example of chromosomal stasis — exceed the global median once microchromosome dynamics are resolved. Read it on bioRxiv.

title: Sean Chien lead-authors chromosome-level long-armed scarab genome
body: Sean Chien's reference genome of the endemic, endangered long-armed scarab Cheirotonus formosanus is now published in Ecology and Evolution. The paper reports a putative Y-linked scaffold and reconstructs the demographic history of this Taiwanese conservation target. DOI: 10.1002/ece3.73483

title: Sean Chien's first PhD paper out in Journal of Evolutionary Biology
body: Sean Chien & Heath Blackmon — "Chromosomal Rearrangements: Tempo and Mode of Karyotype Evolution in Scarabaeoidea" is now published in the Journal of Evolutionary Biology. The paper reconstructs fission/fusion dynamics and sex-chromosome–autosome fusions across the scarab superfamily. DOI: 10.1093/jeb/voag025

title: Megan Copeland coauthors review on salmonid thyroid evolution
body: Megan Copeland is a coauthor on a new review with J. Geoffrey Eales (Manitoba) and Duncan MacKenzie (TAMU) in General and Comparative Endocrinology: "Peripheral and central regulation of thyroid status in teleost fish with particular reference to tetraploid juvenile salmonids and Parr-Smolt transformation." The work synthesizes how genome duplication in salmonids shapes deiodinase paralogs and thyroid regulation. DOI: 10.1016/j.ygcen.2026.114929

title: 10 Papers in One Week: A Progress Report
body: I told the lab we were going to submit 10 papers this week. We submitted four, which, for anyone keeping score, is still an absurd amount of work for one week. Beyond the submissions, the progress people made on other manuscripts and analyses was just as impressive. Wildly proud of this group.

title: Lab paper sprint: 10 manuscripts targeted for submission
body: The week of March 16th we are launching a lab-wide paper sprint with a goal of submitting or resubmitting 10 manuscripts. We have multiple graduate students and undergraduates with papers that are virtually complete — this is a coordinated push to get them across the finish line. We will post updates here as each paper is submitted or resubmitted.

title: Dr. Megan Copeland successfully defends dissertation
body: Megan Copeland defended her PhD dissertation on February 19th, capping years of research on genome assembly, annotation, and the evolution of genome structure. Congratulations, Dr. Copeland!

title: Megan Copeland wins Ashworth-Tsutsui Memorial Award for Mentoring
body: Megan Copeland was selected as the 2025–2026 recipient of the Ethel Ashworth-Tsutsui Memorial Award for Mentoring from the Texas A&M College of Arts & Sciences.

title: Megan Copeland awarded U.S. Senator Phil Gramm Doctoral Fellowship
body: Megan Copeland was selected as a 2025 recipient of the prestigious U.S. Senator Phil Gramm Doctoral Fellowship Award, recognizing her outstanding contributions to teaching and research.

title: 'Wright Was Right' wins SSE Presidents' Award for Outstanding Dissertation Paper
body: Our paper on epistasis across more than 1,000 datasets from plants and animals was selected for the 2025 Society for the Study of Evolution Presidents' Award for Outstanding Dissertation Paper — one of the society's top honors.

title: Alfieri wins AGA Outstanding Student-Authored Paper Award
body: James Alfieri's cover article in Journal of Heredity on domestication and hybrid compatibility in landfowl was unanimously selected as the Outstanding 2024 Student-Authored Paper by the American Genetic Association.

title: Dr. Jorja Burch successfully defends dissertation
body: Jorja Burch defended her PhD dissertation on November 15th. Her work provided empirical tests of long-standing evolutionary theory, including the award-winning 'Wright Was Right' paper.
